system.summary: Letter table with several homophones per vowel, about 60 signs, no word division. Some signs carry a raised ring or numeral that belongs to the sign. Two signs stand for doubled letters (Le ll, Lo nn); in the 2 Aug letter two more (ss, ff) by context. No nomenclator signs found.
system.doubled_letters: Le = ll, Lo = nn; in 2 Aug N13 = ss and N18 = ff from context; mm, other ff and ss written out
system.notes: No sign for h yet: plain x reads a in most places and h in three (Rochelle, chemin, hors); a shape split is suspected but not settled. Not the Charles V to Saint-Mauris table of Pierrot et al. (HistoCrypt 2023).

prior_solution.where: Not in the catalogue, the leads, the decode queue or open PRs (checked 3 Nov 2026). Web searches found no edition or decipherment of these Estense letters; Pierrot et al., HistoCrypt 2023 covers a different table. British Library copies of Saint-Mauris's letters to Covos (1547-1548) were not opened.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT chose the item from its own sweep of IIIF collections and set the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, solved, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (blind transcription merge, simulated annealing on French 4-grams, held-out test, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: cc. 1-11 and 22-23 fetched from the Estense IIIF service by tiles, one request at a time.
10 Jan 1548 (cc. 3r-4r): two independent blind sign passes, 96.0% agreement, disagreements settled on crops.
Ciphertext-only annealing over sign-to-letter maps, scored with 4-grams of 16th-century French; 3 of 10 restarts reached the same table, which read as French.
The contemporary gloss over 3r row 2 gives 15 sign values; the unseeded solve agrees on 13.
9 values corrected from the reading; table frozen on 10 Jan only as key_frozen.tsv.
Held-out 2 Aug 1548, blind transcription, frozen table: 4-gram -4.171 per letter against max -5.189 for 200 shuffled tables; 132 of 179 words verbatim.
Independent check (VERIFY.md): decryptions rebuilt byte-identical; blind second reading of 9r L01-L16; four key values contradicted by the text and one merge of shape classes found.
Fixes on crops: 8 split into 8 (q) and N15 (b); Le split into Le (ll) and Lo (nn); the 2 Aug gamma kept apart (yg); the 2 Aug R renamed N20 (x). N6 set to m in key.tsv; the frozen table unchanged.
Solve rerun on the fixed 10 Jan transcription, 10 restarts: no restart returned the table; the best is a text that does not read.
Catalogue and repository checked; several web searches; no edition found.

outcome.method_basis: Simulated annealing on 4-grams of 16th-century French over the 10 Jan 1548 letter, with no clear text; a contemporary gloss of one row agrees on 13 of 15 values. The table was frozen and tested on the held-out letter of 2 Aug 1548.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Two of four cipher letters are read in part (340 of 435 words verbatim, 78.2%); the other two are not transcribed, so their length is unknown.

texts.label: 10 Jan 1548, cc. 3r-4r
texts.summary: Pignatelli and a reprisal; a courier from Dorsey and Gonzaga's enterprise against Mirandola, whose count has added a hundred arquebusiers to his guard; the French fear a castle; about 1,500 soldiers sent from La Rochelle to Scotland; some hope of peace, and advice to temporise.
texts.note: Words 256: 208 verbatim (81.2%), 30 with marked repairs, 4 proposed, 14 holes. Key: key.tsv, built on this letter.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Paragraphs 2-6 make coherent sense: the courier from Dorsey, Mirandola and the hundred arquebusiers, the castle, La Rochelle to Scotland, the peace and the advice to temporise. Weak places: paragraph 1 is a skeleton between holes (pecesarlauest, fdeluialion, estronestdauandre); there is a 'deqtdeborqonnancieneuendant' hole in the temporise sentence; the last paragraph (captain of Finale) is mostly holes. Five q-for-b repairs come from the 8/N15 merge. (This review predates the sign fixes of 3 Nov 2026; the q-for-b repairs are now verbatim b. The grade was not redone.)

texts.label: 2 Aug 1548, cc. 9r-9v (held out)
texts.summary: Henri II's journey into Piedmont with ambassadors following the court; the French say they will hinder the passage of 'monsieur nostre prince' but cannot; Gonzaga should beware of surprises and guard his person; the journey is to hearten the French party in Italy; a defensive league with money for next year.
texts.note: Words 179 with the frozen table: 132 verbatim (73.7%), 41 with marked repairs, 2 proposed, 4 holes. With values set after the test (key.tsv; not a test): 160 verbatim (89.4%).

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Paragraph 2 reads well throughout: the prince's passage, guarding his person, heart for the French party in Italy. Weak places: 'et sera qu'on la [?fanterie] demeure ... avec aultres ambassadeurs' makes no sense; holes after 'par ou ie' (loureroies, perhaps 'loueroie') and after 'aisemant'; paragraph 3 opens with a hole (sdla), so the antecedent of 'avec lequel' and the league partner are lost; 'ne' read as 'na' and 'defansive' are artefacts of the n/y merge. 26 letters come from signs not in the table and are filled from context. (This review predates the sign fixes of 3 Nov 2026: the hole after 'aisemant' now reads 'aller d'austant que', and the n/y artefacts are gone. The grade was not redone.)

gaps.item: Second blind reading of 9r L17-L18 and 9v
gaps.detail: Only 9r L01-L16 has an independent second blind reading. The agent that made the fixes had seen the key, so it could not read blind.
Some may be transcription slips, others wrong or missing values.

gaps.item: Sign for h; x against h
gaps.detail: x reads a in most places and h in three; a shape split is suspected but not settled on the crops. N19 (3 places) and L1 (1) have no value.

gaps.item: Values set after the held-out test
gaps.detail: N12-N18, N20, yg and Lo come from reading 2 Aug itself and are untested; the 1547 and 12 Mar 1548 letters would test them.
Dorsey, Pignatelli, the La Rochelle to Scotland sailing and the defensive league are checked only in outline.
Editions of Saint-Mauris's correspondence and the British Library letters to Covos were not opened.
